call_points.text: Leisure strategy unchanged at 20% of the portfolio despite strong resort performance.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for substantial completion by FY27 end; step-change in growth from FY2028.
Taj Delhi airport: minimum 70 rooms to launch in Q4FY27, balance within Q1FY28.
South Goa construction hoped to start by end of this quarter; design and contracting ready.
Udaipur expansion awaits local authority and army cantonment approvals; clarity expected over next quarter or two.
Commercial portfolio 91% committed after a 66,000 sq ft LOI at Bangalore.
Yearly rentals give eligibility for ₹2,000 Cr LRD; lease rentals cover the entire interest cost.
Management declined to guide on Q2 occupancy, citing day-to-day volatility from the West Asia conflict.
Deloitte lease at Westin Hyderabad Hitec renewed for one more year; terms revisited by end of fiscal.
Planned capex of approximately **₹3,000 Cr** over FY27 to FY29 across hospitality and commercial real estate portfolios, largely funded through internal accruals.
Average cost of finance remains stable at **7.48%** as of March 2026.
CIGNUS II Powai on track for FY27 end substantial completion, despite minor labour availability pressures.
Ritz-Carlton Hyderabad fit-out cost expected to be close to **₹560 Cr**, back-ended after getting possession in Q4 FY28.
Company took an enabling approval for debt raise of up to **₹1,000 Cr**, with no immediate plan to raise incremental debt.

timeline.summary: Chalet Hotels approved the acquisition of Seasons Hotels Private Limited for ₹171 Cr to enter Udaipur.
Chalet Hotels received requests from Content Properties and Sycamore Properties for reclassification from promoter group to public.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹558.22 Cr (+6.9% YoY), net profit ₹163 Cr (+31.6% YoY).
Chalet Hotels reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹571 Cr and net profit of ₹163 Cr, alongside strategic expansion in Hyderabad and Udaipur.
Chalet Hotels Limited shared the earnings call recording for Q4FY26 & FY26 results on May 15, 2026, via **Bernadette Christabelle Baptista**, CFO.
Chalet Hotels hosted its Q4FY26 earnings call on May 15, 2026, reporting robust full-year cash flows and outlining a ₹3,000 Cr capex plan for FY27-FY29.
On May 26, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled in favour of Chalet Hotels, setting aside the Bombay High Court's land restoration order for Four Points by Sheraton Navi Mumbai and upholding regularisation.
On its 30 July 2026 Q1FY27 call, Chalet Hotels reported core revenue up 10% to ₹514 Cr and EBITDA margin up 231 bps to 46.7%, and outlined about ₹3,000 Cr of capex over FY27-FY29.
